haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized and is not forwarded. No counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: Up to 100 per minute in total, since all of a customer's keys share one counter. Across a minute boundary, up to about 200 in a few seconds.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. Nothing is added to the counter for a rejected request.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The request was counted before forwarding, and the count is not refunded.
haiku-low.q6: It fails open: the request is forwarded anyway, ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and the response has no X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: NOT STATED, since no Enterprise limit is set yet.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, as one counter per customer per minute shared by all keys. A 120-second TTL, set when the counter is created, removes old counts.
haiku-low.q9: Each minute uses its own counter for the current minute, so the budget effectively resets at each new minute (fixed window).
haiku-low.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs as one atomic step in Redis, so no other command can run in the middle of it.
haiku-low.q11: Redis returns the seconds left in the minute, rounded up to a whole second and never less than 1.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store. The client gets no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers.

sonnet.q1: Gateway returns 401 Unauthorized and does not forward. No counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Total is limited to the customer's single per-minute budget (e.g. 100/min for Standard); all of a customer's keys share one counter. Enterprise limit not set.
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The backend never sees it (not forwarded).
sonnet.q4: No. Nothing is added to the counter on a rejected request.
sonnet.q5: Yes. It was counted before forwarding and is not refunded.
sonnet.q6: It fails open: the request is forwarded to the backend anyway, ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and the backend's response is returned without X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: not decided/not set (NOT STATED as a number); what happens to Enterprise requests is an open question.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, one counter per customer per minute, shared by all instances. A 120-second TTL, set when the counter is created, makes Redis delete old counters.
sonnet.q9: The window is a fixed per-minute window; a new minute uses a new counter, so budget resets when the minute changes (minute decided by Redis's clock). Old counters expire via TTL.
sonnet.q10: The check-and-increment is a Lua script that Redis runs as one atomic step, so two instances cannot both read 99 and both be allowed.
sonnet.q11: It is the seconds left in the current minute (per Redis clock), rounded up to a whole second, never less than 1.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether it retries the store; the document only says it fails open after one 50 ms wait. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, only the backend's response.
